### Tiberian Sun with Firestorm (`cnc-ts`)

Written in batch R2 preparation, before any `cnc-ts` unit is coded, from the Tiberian Sun and Firestorm manual scans, the wiki's transcripts of both, the unreleased Ultimate Collection manual, the manual quote boxes on the unit pages, and CnCNet's copy of the rules files for the damage table.

- **No in-game role line.** Hovering over a build icon shows only the price (Tiberian Sun manual, Building, PDF page 38). There are no unit tooltips with a job or a matchup.
- **Official text: the two manuals.** Units have no designation, so the paragraph is the unit's official one-line description.
  - Tiberian Sun manual (1999), Classified Intelligence Report: one paragraph per unit, no stat words. GDI units are on PDF pages 11 to 15, Nod units on 16 to 20. PDF: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/be/Manual_Tiberian_Sun.pdf/revision/latest. Transcript: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Command_%26_Conquer:_Tiberian_Sun_manual (it leaves out the interface and key sections; read those in the PDF).
  - Firestorm manual (2000), Arsenal Updates (PDF pages 7 to 10): a paragraph with Range, Armour and Weapon stat words for each of the six new units (Mobile EMP, Juggernaut, the two mobile factories, Limpet Drone, Mobile Stealth Generator, Reaper), and update notes for the Jump Jet Infantry, the Mobile Sensor Array (called Deployable Sensor Array there) and the EMP Cannon. PDF: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/3/37/Manual_Firestorm.pdf/revision/latest. Transcript: https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Command_%26_Conquer:_Tiberian_Sun_-_Firestorm_manual (it leaves out the new keys and the random-map options of Game Enhancements, PDF page 10).
  - Where a Firestorm update changes a unit, the 1999 paragraph is out of date on that point: Jump Jets now detect cloaked units while flying and move faster; the sensor array also finds drones and mines; the EMP Cannon also destroys drones and brings tunnelling units up.
  - The Ultimate Collection's English manual (Tiberian Sun with Firestorm, never released) reprints shortened versions of both sets of paragraphs and adds no role words: https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/1/13/CCUC-TS-pcMANOLeUS.pdf/revision/latest. Read the two shipped manuals first.
  - The PDFs are the publisher's manuals, not pages of the wiki that hosts them, so they never count toward the sources rule's third page of the same site. Cite them as kind official; cite a transcript or a unit page as kind wiki, with a note that it copies the manual.
  - The stat words of the Firestorm units are grades, not the game's types or band data (the manual calls the Mobile EMP lightly armoured; its infobox and the rules give heavy). The Weapon word is only a name.
- **How to cite.** Every base-game unit page read, apart from the Attack Buggy's, has a quote box credited to the Tiberian Sun manual: cite that page, kind wiki, with a note naming the manual. The Firestorm unit pages (Juggernaut (Firestorm), Limpet drone, Mobile EMP, Mobile stealth generator, Reaper (Firestorm), Mobile war factory) have no quote box: cite the Firestorm transcript. Cite a PDF, kind official, only for text no wiki page copies (the interface and key sections, Game Enhancements), and check those paraphrases by hand: the copy-check cannot read a PDF.
- **No official line at all:** the Attack Buggy. Its page says both the Tiberian Sun and First Decade manuals left it out, and the Ultimate Collection manual has no entry either. Step 1 gives it nothing.
- **Roles step 1.** A paragraph names a role only through a label or alias that describes the unit's own job, in any word form; the unit's name counts when it names that job.
  - Names a role: anti-air, the Jump Jet Infantry (an anti-air defence); scout, the Hover MLRS (ideal for scouting) and the Attack Cycle (used mainly for scouting), and the Limpet Drone (it relays recon data), each still subject to scout's requires; siege, the Artillery (an artillery platform) and the Orca Bomber (its name); transport, the Amphibious APC and the Subterranean APC (APC: armoured personnel carrier); support, the Medic (its name) and the Mobile Repair Vehicle (it repairs vehicles); engineer, the Engineer (its name); infiltrator, the Mutant Hijacker (its name); logistics, the Harvester (its name) and the Weed Eater (it harvests veins).
  - The Orca Carryall's paragraph calls it a transport aircraft, but it lifts one vehicle, so transport's requires (two or more seats) fails and step 1 skips it; it is unarmed, so steps 2 and 6 decide.
  - Name no role: the Light Infantry, Cyborg, Disc Thrower, Ghostalker, Wolverine, Titan (assault and defence: assault on its own names nothing, as in batch R1), Disruptor, Mobile Sensor Array, Orca Fighter (an attack aircraft), Tick Tank and Stealth Tank (light battle tanks), Banshee, Devil's Tongue, Cyborg Commando, Mobile EMP, Juggernaut (its support fire means firepower), the two mobile factories and the Mobile Stealth Generator.
  - A label on one weapon is not the unit's job: the Mammoth Mk. II's anti-aircraft missile launcher and the Reaper's anti-personnel net launcher count only for that weapon, at roles.secondary step 3.
- **Shared units.** The Light Infantry, Engineer, Harvester and MCV paragraphs appear under both sides with the same job, so they are official text for the shared entries. Both manuals print the Mobile Sensor Array only under GDI, but both sides build it in 2.03 (the rules give it both owners, and the Nod war factory and Mobile sensor array pages list it for Nod): the manual's side is not the faction, and its paragraph counts for the shared entry. The Limpet Drone's Firestorm paragraph is headed for both arsenals.
- **Strong against and weak against (roles step 4 and roles.secondary).** No separate lines. Read the paragraph.
  - Strong, naming a kind of target: the Wolverine (large groups of infantry), the Rocket Infantry (vehicles, structures, infantry and aircraft; vehicles named first), the Cyborg Commando (vehicles, infantry and structures), the Harpy (infantry, then lightly armoured vehicles) and the Devil's Tongue (infantry and structures). The Hover MLRS paragraph says its rockets hit air and land equally well: that tells what it can hit, not a strength. The Mobile EMP's pulse disables vehicles; that is a tool, not damage.
  - Target words: vehicles, tanks and armour mean armour; infantry and soldiers mean infantry; aircraft and air mean air. Structures, bases and defences match none of the three anti roles.
  - Weak points in the paragraphs name no kind of target (the Juggernaut is helpless while packed up and has a minimum range; the Mobile EMP has a short reach and a long recharge; the Stealth Tank uncloaks to fire; the Attack Cycle gives up armour for speed), so none drops an anti role.
- **Step 4 bonus from the game data: yes, unlike Red Alert 1.** Each weapon's warhead (in brackets in the infobox attack line) has a damage share against each of the five armour types: none, wood, light, heavy and concrete. The Cyborg (Tiberian Sun) page's armour line gives every warhead's share against light; CnCNet's copy of the rules (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CnCNet/cncnet-ts-client-package/master/INI/Rules.ini) gives the whole table, and it matches that line.
  - More than full damage: Fire (six times against none, about one and a half against wood), RailShot (the Mammoth Mk. II: double against none, a little less against wood and light), RailShot2 (the Ghost Stalker: one and a half against light, about a third more against wood and a tenth more against heavy), ORCAAP (the Orca Fighter: one and a half against light), ORCAHE (the Orca Bomber: double against none), PlasmaWH (the Cyborg Commando: three and a half against none, falling to one and a half against heavy) and WebMass (the Reaper's net, six times against none, but it does no damage, so it is a tool).
  - No bonus: SA, HollowPoint, AP, HE, ARTYHE, SonicWarhead, Super and IonWH. A warhead's share against prone infantry (ProneDamage) is not a bonus against a kind of target.
  - Armour types and targets (proposal for the lead): none is the standard infantry (also the Mutant Hijacker and the Limpet Drone), so a bonus against none is anti-infantry; heavy is the heavy vehicles and the Cyborg Commando, so a bonus there is anti-armour; light covers light vehicles but also the Cyborg, Jump Jet Infantry, Ghost Stalker, Reaper and every aircraft, so a bonus against light alone counts as anti-armour with an uncertain entry naming those; wood and concrete are buildings (plus the Attack Cycle, Hover MLRS and Mobile Sensor Array on wood), so no anti role.
- **Not official.** The UnitBox `role` field (for example, the Stealth tank page's anti-armour and anti-air hit-and-run line), the one-line `desc` under each unit on the war factory and other production pages, the infobox notes and the prose are the wiki's words. A quote box of a voice line is not the manual. CNCNZ's Tiberian Sun unit pages (the copy-check cache holds the Nod one) reword the manuals: kind guide. Prima's official strategy guide was not read.
- **Official site.** Westwood's Tiberian Sun site (http://www.westwood.com/games/ccuniverse/tiberiansun/) has a 1999 Wayback snapshot, but web.archive.org reset the connection from this session, so whether it had unit profiles is unchecked.

### Tiberian Sun with Firestorm (`cnc-ts`)

Written in batch R2 preparation, before any `cnc-ts` unit is coded, for patch 2.03 in Firestorm mode. Sources: the Tiberian Sun and Firestorm manuals and the Tiberian Sun reference card (PDF links under Official role lines; the reference card is https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/8/89/Tiberian_Sun_-_English_-_Reference_Card.pdf/revision/latest), the Command & Conquer Wiki pages named below (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/<Title>, read through the API), ModEnc pages read from the copy-check cache (ModEnc refused direct requests from this session), and CnCNet's copy of the game's rules files, Rules.ini with Firestrm.ini on top (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CnCNet/cncnet-ts-client-package/master/INI/Rules.ini and .../INI/Firestrm.ini; see the research notes for what that copy is). Code files do not exist for this game: Westwood's Tiberian Sun source was never released.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit. Move and attack by clicking, stop (S), guard (G: follow and protect a chosen friendly unit), scatter (X), force-fire (Ctrl), force-move (Alt), rally points for factories (Ctrl+Alt), way-points (W), looped way-points for patrols (Shift), a guard patrol that fires at any enemy met along the way-points (Ctrl+Alt on a way-point), teams (Ctrl and a number), select all (E), next and previous unit (N, B), and in Firestorm select all of one type (T; patch 2.00 added the key) (Tiberian Sun manual, PDF pages 36 to 51; Firestorm manual, PDF page 10; [Tiberian Sun patch 2.00](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Tiberian_Sun_patch_2.00)). There are no stances and no retreat, reinforce or separate attack-move order.
  - Deploying is done by clicking the selected unit itself (manual entries for the Tick Tank, Artillery, MCV and Amphibious APC). It is not an order: on a transport it unloads the riders (universal key); on any other unit what it does is that unit's ability (the Tick Tank digging in, the Artillery and Juggernaut planting, the Mobile Sensor Array and Mobile Stealth Generator switching on, the MCV and the two mobile factories becoming buildings).
  - The Medic and the Mobile Repair Vehicle heal or repair nearby units by themselves when set to guard (manual); that belongs to their own repair ability.
- **Veterancy** (`earn-veterancy`): every unit that fights, except those below. Two ranks, veteran then elite, each earned by destroying enemies worth more than a multiple of the unit's own price; a crate can also promote ([Veterancy](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy)).
  - **Numbers depend on the mode.** The Veterancy page gives ten times the price and, per rank, a quarter more damage, a quarter more armour, a fifth faster firing and three tenths more speed. Those are the Tiberian Sun mode values (Rules.ini). Firestrm.ini, read on top in Firestorm mode, lowers the multiple to five and raises the damage and armour lifts to half and the firing lift to three tenths. Where a rank's numbers matter, use the Firestorm values and add an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree that names the Veterancy page.
  - **Elite extras** (the Veterancy page's table and the rules' EliteAbilities): scattering from fire (Light Infantry, Disc Thrower, Rocket Infantry), radar invisibility (Jump Jet Infantry, Orca Bomber, Banshee), stealth sensors (Titan, Tick Tank, Juggernaut), self-repair (Hover MLRS, Artillery, Devil's Tongue), exploding on death (Stealth Tank, Mobile Stealth Generator), crushing infantry (Attack Buggy, Reaper), vein immunity (Attack Cycle; also listed for the Wolverine, which already has it), toughness (Cyborg). The Disruptor explodes when elite in Tiberian Sun mode but is faster instead in Firestorm (Firestrm.ini; [Disruptor (Tiberian Sun)](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Disruptor_(Tiberian_Sun))). All of these stay with veterancy: no armour model, sensor trait, mobility trait or on_death outcome at stock; mention them in notes.
  - **Elite weapons** (Paired entries): the Light Infantry's better rifle and the Tick Tank's double-shot cannon only hit harder, so they go in the stock weapon's summary. The Attack Cycle's elite missiles (the Hover MLRS's) can also hit aircraft, while its stock missile cannot (the rules give the stock projectile no anti-air flag; the [Stealth tank](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth_tank_(Tiberian_Sun)) page agrees that cycles fire at aircraft only when elite): an acquired weapon with Elite rank as its condition, linking `earn-veterancy`.
  - **Cannot rank up:** the Cyborg Commando, Ghost Stalker and Mammoth Mk. II (Veterancy page; Umagon is campaign-only); say so in weaknesses. The rules also mark the Mutant Hijacker, Limpet Drone, Mobile EMP, Mobile Stealth Generator and both mobile factories as untrainable; none of those fights with a damaging weapon, so name it in notes only.
- **No garrisons**: buildings never take infantry in to fight; garrisoning starts with Red Alert 2 ([Garrisoning](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning)). Infantry enter buildings only through actions of their own (the Engineer's capture and repair, the Ghost Stalker's C4); the Mutant Hijacker enters vehicles. Record each on its unit.
- **Transports** (universal keys for boarding and unloading; one seat passive per carrier, Paired entries):
  - The Amphibious APC and the Subterranean APC each carry five infantry (manual; rules). No page read shows riders firing out, so the seats are passenger-cargo and the passive links `carry-passengers`. The Amphibious APC cannot unload while on water (manual); the Subterranean APC cannot come up under pavement, a Tiberium field or uneven ground ([Subterranean APC](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Subterranean_APC)).
  - The Orca Carryall (GDI) lifts one ground vehicle, never infantry directly; an APC with riders can be lifted ([Orca Carryall](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Orca_Carryall); manual). Picking up and dropping are universal keys; the one-vehicle hold is its seat passive (`carry-passengers`), as for the Red Alert 3 Twinblade's vehicle lift.
  - No page read says what happens to riders when a transport is destroyed: write nothing about them unless the unit's own page does.
- **Crew survivors** (no pattern): the rules have a Crewed flag for vehicles whose crew can escape, but no source read gives Tiberian Sun's chance or says what climbs out. So a crewed vehicle takes the decision-3C default (bail-out, basis proposal) unless its own page shows survivors, and says in on_death.notes that the rules mark it crewed. Crewed in the rules copy: MCV, Harvester, Weed Eater, Tick Tank, Artillery, Juggernaut, Hover MLRS, Mobile EMP, Mobile Sensor Array, both mobile factories and all five aircraft. Not crewed (no survivor): Titan, Wolverine, Mammoth Mk. II, Disruptor, Amphibious APC, Subterranean APC, Attack Buggy, Attack Cycle, Stealth Tank, Devil's Tongue, Mobile Repair Vehicle, Mobile Stealth Generator, Reaper and Limpet Drone.
- **Repair, rearming and healing at buildings** (no pattern; leave all of these off):
  - The Service Depot repairs vehicles and aircraft for credits (manual; [Service depot](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Service_depot_(Tiberian_Sun))). Only GDI has one: the depot's own page, the manual's list of Nod buildings and the rules all leave Nod out (the Nod war factory page's infobox still names it), so Nod vehicles are mended only by the Mobile Repair Vehicle. A vehicle on the depot can also be sold. A depot also removes an attached Limpet Drone, and so can a Mobile Repair Vehicle (Firestorm manual; [Limpet drone](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Limpet_drone)).
  - Each side's Helipad builds and rearms aircraft, one aircraft per pad; capturing a pad captures the aircraft parked on it ([Helipad](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Helipad_(Tiberian_Sun))).
  - Buildings are repaired with the sidebar wrench for credits (manual); an Engineer sent into a damaged friendly building restores it fully, which is the Engineer's own ability.
  - Units that repair others record it on themselves (`repair-allies`): the Medic heals infantry and the Mobile Repair Vehicle repairs vehicles (manual).
  - Stock self-repair (armour model `self-repair`; the rules' flag heals up to half health): the Harvester and the Mammoth Mk. II (the war factory pages), the Medic ([Medic](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Medic_(Tiberian_Sun))) and the Weed Eater (rules). Elite self-repair is veterancy, above.
  - Healing in Tiberium is not self-repair: the Cyborg, Cyborg Commando, Ghost Stalker, Mutant Hijacker and Reaper mend while standing in a Tiberium field (their pages; rules). Say so in armour.notes.
- **Ammunition** (resource `limited-ammo`, not an ability): the Orca Fighter, Orca Bomber, Harpy and Banshee carry a fixed load and must fly back to a helipad to reload (manual, which says so of every aircraft; rules ammo counts). Code limited-ammo on each and leave the trip off. A pad serves one aircraft, and aircraft built while every pad is taken fly in from the map edge to the primary pad (Helipad page); that limit is shared by every aircraft type and grows with each pad, so the aircraft stay availability open.
- **Crushing** (mobility trait `crush`, not an ability): vehicles the rules mark as crushers run over infantry: the MCV, Harvester, Weed Eater, Amphibious APC, Subterranean APC, Titan, Juggernaut, Mammoth Mk. II, Disruptor, Tick Tank, Stealth Tank, Artillery, Devil's Tongue, Mobile Repair Vehicle, Mobile Sensor Array, Mobile EMP, Mobile Stealth Generator and both mobile factories. Not crushers: the Wolverine, Attack Cycle, Hover MLRS and Limpet Drone, and the Attack Buggy and Reaper, which crush only when elite.
  - Vehicles never crush vehicles ([Mammoth Mk. II](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Mammoth_Mk._II): the engine does not allow it). Player units do not go out of their way to crush infantry (the rules switch that off for players); a move or force-move through infantry does it.
  - Uncrushable infantry say so in strengths (`immune:crush`): the Cyborg, Cyborg Commando and Jump Jet Infantry (their infoboxes) and the Mutant Hijacker (rules). A crusher smaller than large still gets the trait, with the size break recorded in atypical, as in batch R1; the trait never decides a size.
- **Going prone** (no pattern, not an armour model): infantry drop to the ground when shot at, giving up speed for toughness ([Light infantry](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Light_infantry_(Tiberian_Sun))); each warhead sets its own share against prone soldiers (rules). The rules mark the Jump Jet Infantry, Cyborg and Cyborg Commando fearless, so they do not drop. Mention it in armour.notes only where it matters; never code damage-reduction for it.
- **Damage slows units down** (no pattern): units in the yellow and red move and work worse (manual, Check-up), and ModEnc's Speed page puts a damaged driving vehicle at three quarters speed. Leave it off; speed bands use full health. The Cyborg dropping its legs when badly hurt belongs to the Cyborg ([Cyborg](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Cyborg_(Tiberian_Sun))).
- **Ground and speed** (no pattern): units reach their listed speed only on roads and pavement; open ground slows soldiers a little and tracked or wheeled vehicles more (rules land table; manual, Pavement; [Pavement](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Pavement)). Pavement also stops burrowing units and craters (manual). How this sets speed bands is under the research notes; it is never a unit's trait.
- **Tiberium, veins and lifeforms** (map hazards, no pattern; leave off):
  - Green Tiberium hurts infantry who stay in it, and blue Tiberium explodes when shot (manual, PDF page 40); the rules also let infantry change into visceroids. Immune in the rules: the Cyborg, Cyborg Commando, Ghost Stalker, Mutant Hijacker and Reaper; say so in strengths (`immune:toxic`; the same flag covers Tiberium gas).
  - Veinhole veins attack units that are not immune. The rules make every ground infantry type, the Harvester, Weed Eater, Wolverine, Attack Buggy and Reaper immune (the elite Attack Cycle too). No word-list term covers it: mention it in notes.
  - Firestorm's random-map options add veinholes, Tiberium lifeforms (visceroids, fiends, floaters) and random ion storms (Firestorm manual, PDF page 10).
- **Crates** (a multiplayer option; picking one up is a universal key): leave every crate effect off. A crate can give money, a veterancy rank, an armour, firepower or speed bonus to units near it, full health, a free vehicle or infantry squad, a view of the whole map or a re-shrouded map, a missile strike, or cloaking for nearby units, and the bad ones explode, burn, release Tiberium gas or spread Tiberium ([Crate](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Crate); rules). A unit cloaked only by a crate gets no cloak.
- **Side-wide powers and buildings** (left off every unit; none gives named unit types a new button, so no ability has source commander-power):
  - GDI: the Ion Cannon, Hunter-Seeker droid and, in Firestorm, Drop Pods with veteran infantry, all from plugs on the Upgrade Center ([Upgrade center](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Upgrade_center), [Drop Pod](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Drop_Pod)); the Firestorm Defense, which turns the Firestorm walls into a barrier that destroys anything crossing it, aircraft and missiles included ([Firestorm generator](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Firestorm_generator)).
  - Nod: the Multi-missile and the Chemical Missile from the Missile Silo (the chemical one needs veins brought by the Weed Eater to a Tiberium Waste Facility) ([Multi missile](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Multi_missile), [Chemical missile](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Chemical_missile)); the Hunter-Seeker from the Temple of Nod; the Stealth Generator, which cloaks everything in a wide bubble while it has power ([Stealth generator](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth_generator)).
  - Both: the EMP Cannon's pulse, which stops vehicles, structures and cyborgs (the Cyborg Commando included) for a while, friend or foe, brings tunnelling units up and sinks a Hover MLRS caught over water (an Amphibious APC stays afloat); airborne aircraft are unaffected ([Electromagnetic pulse cannon](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Electromagnetic_pulse_cannon)). The Hunter-Seeker droid finds a target by itself and only the Firestorm Defense stops it ([Hunter-Seeker droid](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Hunter-Seeker_droid)); it is a power, not a unit to research.
  - Mention an effect in notes where it matters for a matchup.
- **Cloaking, burrowing and detection** (per unit, apart from two engine defaults):
  - The Stealth Tank cloaks itself and must uncloak to fire (manual): `cloak`. Units hidden only by a Stealth Generator or a deployed Mobile Stealth Generator get no cloak of their own; the Mobile Stealth Generator records its field as its ability.
  - Two Nod vehicles tunnel, the Subterranean APC and Devil's Tongue (`burrow`, mobility trait burrow): unseen underground, they cannot go down or come up under pavement, Tiberium fields or uneven ground ([Subterranean APC](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Subterranean_APC), [Devil's Tongue](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Devil%27s_Tongue_(Tiberian_Sun))), and an EMP forces them up. ModEnc's Locomotor page says the tunnelling movement is used only for longer trips.
  - Detectors (sensor trait `detector`): the Mobile Sensor Array once deployed (cloaked and tunnelling units; in Firestorm also drones and mines) and, in Firestorm, the Jump Jet Infantry while flying (Firestorm manual; [Stealth](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth); rules). The elite sensors of the Titan, Tick Tank and Juggernaut stay with veterancy.
  - Engine defaults that give no unit the detector trait: infantry reveal a cloaked enemy at very close range, and buildings with sensors (Radar, Component Tower, EMP Cannon, Upgrade Center, Temple of Nod, Stealth Generator, Tiberium Waste Facility) reveal cloaked units near them (manual, Stealth Tank entry; Stealth tank page; Stealth page).
  - Radar invisibility (the Harpy and the Mobile Sensor Array at stock; the Jump Jet Infantry, Orca Bomber and Banshee when elite) only keeps the unit off the enemy's radar map; eyes still see it. Give it no stealth trait and add a fit_note at sensors/traits, as for the Red Alert 2 NightHawk.
- **Shroud, fog and radar** (no pattern): black shroud covers unexplored ground and each unit lifts it within its sight; it does not grow back (manual; rules). Fog of war is a skirmish and multiplayer checkbox, off by default (reference card; ModEnc FogOfWar; rules). The radar map needs a powered Radar; low power switches it off (manual). Aircraft have very short sight in the rules.
- **Base power** (no pattern): low power slows production, shuts the radar, and switches off base defences and the Stealth Generator (manual; Stealth generator page). No unit depends on power, so nothing here is `depend-on-relay`.
- **Engineers, capture and hijacking**: not game-wide. The Engineer (shared) captures enemy buildings, fully repairs friendly ones and repairs bridges through their repair huts, and is used up each time (manual; [Engineer](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Engineer_(Tiberian_Sun))): `capture-structure`, with the rest in its summary. The Mutant Hijacker steals vehicles (`hijack-vehicle`) and the Ghost Stalker plants C4 on buildings: their own abilities.
- **No unit upgrades**: there is no research. GDI's add-ons upgrade buildings only (power turbines, component tower weapons, Upgrade Center plugs; manual, Upgrading Buildings), so no unit links `upgrade-in-field`.
- **Build limits** (availability unique; say so in tier.basis): one at a time for the Cyborg Commando and Mutant Hijacker (manual, Temple of Nod entry), the Mammoth Mk. II (manual), the Ghost Stalker (rules), and both mobile factories (war factory pages).
- **Game-setup options** (leave off): Harvester Truce, under which harvesters cannot be harmed and Hunter-Seekers skip them ([Harvester](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Harvester_(Tiberian_Sun))); redeployable MCV; bases on or off; destroyable bridges; starting units; tech level 1 to 10; fog of war; crates (reference card). Selling a vehicle on a GDI Service Depot is an economy rule.
- **Ion storms** (campaign maps and a Firestorm random-map option; the rules keep random storms off): while a storm lasts, aircraft and Jump Jet Infantry in flight crash, grounded aircraft cannot take off, the Hover MLRS stops and radar fails ([Ion storm](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Ion_storm)). Leave it off; mention it in notes of the units it hits.

registry_findings.current: Light infantry (both sides' basic rifle infantry): speed 5 in the game's rules as the wiki lists them, against 4 for the Titan and 6 for the Tick tank
registry_findings.proposed: "Light infantry (both sides' basic rifle infantry): Speed 5 in the rules (the wiki infobox and CnCNet's copy of rules.ini agree), against 4 for the Titan and 6 for the Tick tank. A unit reaches its Speed only on roads and pavement: on open (clear) ground the rules' land table lets foot soldiers keep 90% of it, tracked and wheeled vehicles 70% (a vehicle with no SpeedType key counts as tracked if it is a crusher and wheeled otherwise, walkers included), amphibious units 80%, and hover and creep units 100% (hover adds a boost on straight runs). Aircraft are not slowed, and jump-jet infantry fly at the global jump-jet speed (14). So the reference's open-ground pace is 5 x 90% = 4.5, and speed_raw = Speed x the unit's clear-ground share / 4.5."
registry_findings.evidence: The listed 5 is right but is not the reference's pace on open ground. (1) https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CnCNet/cncnet-ts-client-package/master/INI/Rules.ini (read 2026-10-24, with INI/Firestrm.ini on top): [E1] Speed=5 (also in the repository's oldest 2022 import), [MMCH] Speed=4, [TTNK] Speed=6, so the infobox figure is confirmed; the land table [Clear] gives Foot 90%, Track 70%, Wheel 70%, Amphibious 80%, Hover 100%, Creep 100%, and [Road] gives 100% to all; the file's own key notes define each share as a percentage of full speed for that movement type; [General] HoverBoost=150%; [JumpjetControls] Speed=14. (2) ModEnc LandTypes and Locomotor (copy-check cache, fetched 2026-10-20/21): the shares apply to units of the matching SpeedType; a Drive, Mech or Walk unit with no SpeedType key is Track if Crusher=yes, else Wheel; ModEnc Speed/In_JumpjetControls: Tiberian Sun jump jets fly at that global speed. notes.other_notes:
- **Version and mode.** Code every unit as patch 2.03 plays in Firestorm mode, where the game reads Firestrm.ini on top of Rules.ini. Where an infobox gives a Tiberian Sun and a Firestorm value (the Stealth Tank's health and sight), take the Firestorm one. Firestorm mode changes, among others: the Banshee's price (1,250, was 1,500) and the Harpy's (800, was 1,000), the Disruptor's speed (5, was 4) and the Jump Jet Infantry's (8, was 5), the Stealth Tank's health and sight, the veterancy numbers, and the Disruptor's elite extra. Patch 2.03 itself raised the Mammoth Mk. II's health ([Tiberian Sun patch 2.03](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Tiberian_Sun_patch_2.03)). The Juggernaut, Mobile EMP, Limpet Drone, Mobile Stealth Generator, Reaper and both mobile factories are Firestorm units: `introduced_in: cnc-ts-firestorm`.
- **The rules copy.** CnCNet's Tiberian Sun client package keeps the game's rules files as text: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CnCNet/cncnet-ts-client-package/master/INI/Rules.ini and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CnCNet/cncnet-ts-client-package/master/INI/Firestrm.ini (read the second on top of the first). Cite it as kind database.
  - It is a maintained copy, not a pristine one. Its history shows CnCNet edits since 2023: the Mammoth Mk. II's weapons reworked (its primary and secondary swapped and the railgun given a two-shot burst), crew and tech-level flags fixed on deployed vehicles, the engineer capture keys commented out for the Vinifera engine extension, plus beacons and Vinifera-only keys. Do not rest those keys on it: take the Mammoth Mk. II's weapon order from the manual and its page. The oldest import in the repository (2022) is older than 2.03 on some keys (the Mammoth Mk. II's health, the Disc Thrower's death blast that patch 1.13 added), so use the current file.
  - Elsewhere it matches the wiki on nearly every value checked: the Light Infantry's speed, sight and reach, the Titan's and Tick Tank's prices, every warhead share in the Cyborg page's armour line, and the Tiberian Sun and Firestorm pairs the infoboxes give (Stealth Tank health and sight, Harpy and Banshee prices, Jump Jet speed). That also shows Firestrm.ini is Westwood's Firestorm file. The disagreements found are a few infobox armour words (armour traps, below).
  - Use it for rules values the wiki leaves out or contradicts. Where it and a wiki disagree on a key CnCNet did not edit, this note proposes that the copy wins, with an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree, as batch R1 did with its reference copy; the lead decides.
- **Speed bands (method; see the registry finding).** The speed-bands list asks for plain open ground, and in this game that is not the listed Speed. The rules' [Clear] land type lets soldiers keep 90% of their Speed, tracked and wheeled vehicles 70%, amphibious units 80%, and hover and creep units 100%; roads and pavement give everyone 100%. A vehicle without a SpeedType key moves as tracked if the rules make it a crusher and as wheeled otherwise (ModEnc Locomotor, cached); the Hover MLRS and Limpet Drone are hover, the Amphibious APC amphibious, the Reaper creep. The Light Infantry's open-ground pace is therefore 5 × 90% = 4.5.
  - speed_raw = Speed × the unit's clear-ground share ÷ 4.5, rounded once to two decimals. Checking in whole leptons (Speed × 256 ÷ 100, fractions dropped, times the share, against the rifleman's 12 × 90%) changes no band.
  - What it gives: Titan 0.62 very slow; Tick Tank, Stealth Tank, Mobile Repair Vehicle, Mobile Stealth Generator and Mobile Sensor Array 0.93 slow; Artillery, Disruptor, Devil's Tongue, Subterranean APC (on the surface), Harvester, Weed Eater and Juggernaut 0.78 slow; Wolverine and Mobile EMP 1.09 medium; Reaper 1.11 medium; Amphibious APC 1.42 medium; Attack Buggy 1.56 and Attack Cycle 1.87 fast; Hover MLRS 1.56 fast; Mammoth Mk. II, MCV and the mobile factories 0.47 very slow. Soldiers keep their plain ratio (Speed 4 is 0.80 slow; the Mutant Hijacker's 7 is 1.40 medium).
  - Hover: the rules add a boost on straight runs (HoverBoost). Band from the range without and with it and take the band nearer medium if it crosses an edge: the Hover MLRS is fast either way; the Limpet Drone (1.78 to 2.67) is fast. ModEnc's remark that hover units run about a third slower than drive units fits Red Alert 2, whose clear ground halves hover speed (ModEnc LandTypes); Tiberian Sun's land table gives hover full speed there, so do not apply it.
  - Walkers (Titan, Wolverine, Juggernaut, Mammoth Mk. II, all on the Mech locomotor): the rules reading above is the default. Two wiki pages disagree (the Titan page says walkers keep a steady speed over any terrain; the Pavement page says walkers gain nothing on pavement), and ModEnc's Locomotor page says the Mech locomotor runs roughly 40% slower than Drive. None of the three is backed by code. Add an uncertain entry at mobility/speed naming them; if the lead prefers the range method, the bands become Titan slow, Wolverine medium, Juggernaut medium and Mammoth Mk. II very slow.
  - Jump Jet Infantry fly at the global jump-jet speed (14 in [JumpjetControls]; ModEnc says Tiberian Sun jump jets use it), not their own Speed, which applies on foot over short hops (Jump jet infantry page). Flying is how they fight, so band from 14: 3.11, very fast, with an uncertain entry naming the Firestorm manual's claim that the new jump jets move faster.
  - Aircraft are not slowed by ground: Orca Fighter 4.44, Banshee 4.00, Carryall 3.56, Harpy 3.11, Orca Bomber 2.67, all very fast.
  - The Subterranean APC and Devil's Tongue travel underground at a speed the engine sets separately (ModEnc Locomotor): band their surface speed and mention the tunnelling in notes.
  - Leave off veteran speed, damaged-vehicle slowdown, prone crawling and the Cyborg's legless crawl.
- **Fist of Nod: settled.** Its gate is the Temple of Nod (t3). The rules give the Fist of Nod the Nod War Factory and the Temple of Nod as prerequisites, and the Mobile War Factory needs the Upgrade Center and the GDI War Factory (both copies of Rules.ini); the [Temple of Nod (Tiberian Sun)](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Temple_of_Nod_(Tiberian_Sun)) page lists the Fist of Nod among what the Temple allows, and the [Mobile war factory](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Mobile_war_factory) infobox lists the Upgrade Center and the Temple, one per side. The [Nod war factory (Tiberian Sun)](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Nod_war_factory_(Tiberian_Sun)) page's Upgrade Center requirement repeats the GDI entry by mistake. Both mobile factories are one per player, need tech level 10, and share one page ('Fist of Nod' redirects to 'Mobile war factory'); record one entry per side.
- **Warheads left out of the damage map** (what they are, from the rules copy):
  - Super: full damage to every armour type, which the rules reserve for special cases. It is the warhead of Nod's Laser Turret and Obelisk of Light, CABAL's laser defences and the Hunter-Seeker droid's blast. No researched unit fires it; a laser that did would take the laser family's default, energy.
  - TankOGas: the debris thrown when vehicles and some objects blow up (wreck pieces, fuel tanks, the Disruptor's and Mammoth's turrets, Tiberium crystals). Not a weapon; at most it goes in on_death.notes.
  - Organic: the Medic's heal. It works only on armour type none, so the Medic cannot heal the Cyborg, Cyborg Commando, Jump Jet Infantry or Ghost Stalker (light or heavy armour). Damage step 1 makes it repair.
  - Shard and Slimer: the Tiberian Fiend's crystal shards and the adult Visceroid's slime. Neither creature can be built.
  - RPG: GDI's RPG upgrade on the Component Tower, a base defence.
  - Fire2: the burning damage of things on fire (fire that does not spread further), with the same shares as Fire. No weapon uses it.
  - Also unmapped and fired by buildable units: Mechanical (the Mobile Repair Vehicle: step 1, repair; it works on any armour but none, and the rules bar it from the Reaper), WebMass (the Reaper's net: no damage, it snares infantry, so step 2), LIMPY (the deployed Limpet Drone: next to no damage, it slows its host, step 2), MobileEMPulse (the Mobile EMP's pulse, whose damage figure is its duration: step 2 gives the emp family's emp). EMPuls (EMP Cannon), SAMWH (SAM sites), Gas (chemical missile clouds) and IonCannonWH belong to buildings and powers.
  - IonWH, which the map lists, is the warhead of ion storm lightning; no unit fires it (the Ion Cannon uses IonCannonWH). It does no harm in the map.
  - Railgun shots (Ghost Stalker, Mammoth Mk. II) carry their damage in a separate key (AmbientDamage) with Damage set to zero; read that one.
- **Shared units and faction traps.** Shared: Light Infantry, Engineer, Harvester, MCV, Mobile Sensor Array and Limpet Drone (Firestorm). The manuals list the Mobile Sensor Array under GDI only, but in 2.03 both sides build it (rules owners in both copies; [Mobile sensor array](https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Mobile_sensor_array); Nod war factory page). GDI only: the Medic, Orca Carryall and Service Depot. Nod only: the Mobile Repair Vehicle. The EMP Cannon is a building both sides have.
- **Not buildable in skirmish** (rules tech level -1; leave out): Umagon, Chameleon Spy, Elite Cadre, the mutants and named heroes of the campaign, the Mammoth Tank, Orca Transport, Dropship, Kodiak, Montauk, Hunter-Seeker droids, visceroids, Tiberian Fiend, Tiberium Floater, Core Defender, the civilian Flame Tank and the Missile Launcher.
- **Tier traps.**
  - Orca Carryall: its infobox says tier 3, but it needs only a Helipad and a Service Depot, and the Depot needs only a War Factory, so its gate is Helipad (t2).
  - The Temple of Nod's and Upgrade Center's infoboxes say tier 4; both map to t3.
  - Gates by the rules: Mobile Repair Vehicle, War Factory (t1); Jump Jet Infantry, Hover MLRS, Juggernaut, Artillery, Mobile Sensor Array and Limpet Drone, Radar (t2); Orca Fighter and Harpy, Helipad (t2); Mobile EMP, Electromagnetic Pulse Cannon (t2); Ghost Stalker, Disruptor, Mammoth Mk. II, MCV, Subterranean APC, Devil's Tongue, Stealth Tank, Reaper, Orca Bomber and Banshee, Tech Center (t3); Fist of Nod, Mutant Hijacker and Cyborg Commando, Temple of Nod (t3); Mobile War Factory, Upgrade Center (t3); Weed Eater, Tiberium Waste Facility (t3); Mobile Stealth Generator, Stealth Generator (t3).
- **Price traps.** The Stealth Tank and the Reaper cost 1,100, just under the high threshold of 1,120: medium as the registry stands. The Orca Bomber and the Mobile Stealth Generator cost exactly 1,600: very high (an edge takes the higher band). The Harpy's and Banshee's infoboxes give both prices: take the Firestorm one (800 and 1,250).
- **Armour traps** (no armour_map; use the armour-class order). The rules' types are none, wood, light, heavy and concrete. Infobox disagreements: the Hover MLRS says Light where the rules say wood; the Wolverine's 'Hardened steel' is lore (rules light); the Tick Tank's infobox leaves the type blank (rules light); the Disc Thrower says N/A (rules none). Wood, a building type, is also on the Attack Cycle, Hover MLRS and Mobile Sensor Array; the Limpet Drone is none.
- **Weapon traps.** The stock Attack Cycle missile cannot hit aircraft (no anti-air flag on its projectile in the rules; the Stealth tank page agrees), though the manual says the cycle hits air and ground: list air only for the elite weapon, with an uncertain entry marked sources_disagree. The Titan fires over walls and cliff edges (Titan page).
- **Sight and reach.** Sight and weapon reach are both in cells (the rules' own key notes), so the off-screen test compares them directly. Aircraft sight is 2 against the rifleman's 5 (short).
- **Role traps.** The Attack Buggy has no manual paragraph. The Orca Carryall fails transport's requires (one vehicle). The Hover MLRS's scout role needs fast: it is fast only by the open-ground method above (plain ratio 1.40 is medium).
- **Page titles** (call the API with redirects=1 and cite the resolved title). No suffix: Tick tank, Mammoth Mk. II, Hover MLRS, Amphibious armored personnel carrier, Subterranean APC, Mobile sensor array, Mobile EMP, Mobile repair vehicle, Limpet drone, Mobile stealth generator, Mobile war factory, Mutant hijacker, Ghost Stalker, Disc thrower, Orca fighter, Orca Carryall, Harpy, Weed eater. '(Tiberian Sun)': Light infantry, Rocket infantry, Jump jet infantry, Medic, Engineer, Cyborg, Cyborg Commando, Titan, Wolverine, Disruptor, Attack buggy, Attack cycle, Stealth tank, Artillery, Devil's Tongue, Banshee, Harvester, Mobile construction vehicle; Orca bomber (Tiberian Sun). '(Firestorm)': Juggernaut, Reaper. Redirects seen: Juggernaut Mk. I, Titan Mk. I, Hover Multiple Launch Rocket System, Wolverine Mk. I, Devil's Tongue subterranean flame tank, Fist of Nod, Radar station. 'Disruptor' alone is a disambiguation page.
- **Access.** The wiki API worked throughout. ModEnc answered 403 to direct requests on 2026-10-24, so ModEnc pages were read from the copy-check cache (.cache/sources/modenc.renegadeprojects.com/). web.archive.org reset the connection. raw.githubusercontent.com worked; the GitHub API and code search are closed to this session.

verdicts.reason: Two runs would be flagged: the tier-trap list repeats an eight-word run of names from the Temple of Nod page, and the registry evidence repeats a six-word data run from Rules.ini.

verdicts.correction: Reorder the names (e.g. 'Fist of Nod, Mutant Hijacker and Cyborg Commando') and write the shares as '90% for soldiers, 70% for tracked and wheeled vehicles'.

missing: Stock death blasts: the Disc Thrower and the Harvester explode with collateral damage at stock (Rules.ini E2 Explodes=yes, HARV Explodes=yes; patch 1.13 page: disc throwers explode on death and damage nearby units; Disc thrower infobox note). Both are death-blast, basis in-game; the notes mention the Disc blast only as a version marker.

Elite exploding (Stealth Tank, Mobile Stealth Generator) is an on_death outcome under docs/fields.md on_death.basis (counts even when it needs veterancy, condition in notes), not a notes-only veterancy perk.
Crew survivors are in the rules: CrewEscape=50%, Crew=E1, Pilot=E1 in [General] (also in the 2022 import), so Crewed vehicles bail out in-game by chance (on-death.json bail-out).
The deployed Mobile Stealth Generator detects cloaked units (Rules.ini [MSTL] Sensors=yes; Stealth page TS list). It belongs in the detector list.

Artillery trap: the wiki infobox (150 damage, cooldown 110) is pre-patch-1.13; the copy has 155mm Damage=115, ROF=150 and ARTYHE 40% vs none with ProneDamage 30% (patch 1.13 page: Artillery fires slower, about 20% less damage, weaker vs infantry). ARTYHE is also the Juggernaut's warhead. Git history: the change entered with client import 6ff3e7a, the same import that brought the 2.03 Mammoth health.
Tick Tank infobox lists elite self-repair, but the rules give TTNK only SENSORS (Veterancy page agrees with the rules); the deployed Tick Tank is a separate building type with concrete armour.

Jump Jet speed disagreement: JJ page infobox air speed 5 (TS) / 8 (FS), land speed 5, 'least mobile air unit', against [JumpjetControls] Speed=14 and ModEnc; needs a sources_disagree entry naming the JJ page.

ModEnc Speed/On_Unit_Types (the page the notes cite for the 3/4 crippled-vehicle rule) also says infantry move at 2/3 of Speed when crawling and 3/2 when not; the speed_reference method neither applies nor rebuts this. If it holds for TS, every vehicle ratio against the rifleman shifts; at least add an uncertain entry.

Sight bands: TS has fog of war off by default (Rules.ini FogOfWar=no; ModEnc FogOfWar: skirmish follows the checkbox) and the shroud never regrows (ShroudGrow=no). docs/fields.md sensors.basis makes the band medium, basis proposal, when a game has no fog, and R1 did that for RA2. The notes must decide this and the off-screen test, and aircraft sight also has AttackingAircraftSightRange=6 and AircraftFogReveal=6.

Elevation bonus: Rules.ini LeptonsPerSightIncrease=2000 and LeptonsPerFireIncrease=2000 (height raises sight and weapon reach), and TrackedUphill/WheeledUphill=.5 slow vehicles on slopes; game-wide terrain mechanics to leave off and mention.
Multi Engineer multiplayer option (patch 1.17 page; Engineer (Tiberian Sun) changelog) changes engineer capture; missing from game-setup options.

Firestorm-only weapon changes that infoboxes show at TS values: Bomb Range 5 to 3 (Orca bomber infobox range 5), Grenade ROF 60 to 80 (Disc thrower infobox cooldown 60), artillery accuracy ([Ballistic] block and BallisticScatter 1.0 to 2.0 in Firestrm.ini; patch 2.00 page notes lower Artillery precision in FS).

Damage-key traps beyond railguns: Devil's Tongue FireballLauncher Damage=0 AmbientDamage=2 (infobox 2 x2 Fire), Disruptor SonicZap Damage=1 AmbientDamage=3 (infobox 4), Reaper QuadLauncher Damage=0 SA whose airburst DualRockets do AP 5 and whose DualCluster projectile has AA=yes (Reaper page: rockets hit ground and air).
Veins: the Jump Jet Infantry is vulnerable (Veinhole page; no ImmuneToVeins) and the Hover MLRS is unaffected per the Veinhole page despite no rules flag.
Ghost Stalker page says a medic is often needed for him, but Organic does 0% to light armour (rules), so the Medic cannot heal him: sources_disagree.

Rules copy history: besides the 2023 edits, master has 2024 changes (KODIAK unit removed, visceroid NonVehicle, warhead list) and 2026-10-08 'Migrate to OpenTS', which rewrote some key notes (Totable replaced TooBigForCarryalls); the file now targets OpenTS/Vinifera. The side-branch commit 5b07e55 called 'Merged Tiberian Sun 2.03 INI files' holds pre-2.03 values (HMEC 800) and must not be used as a 2.03 reference.

Deployed forms are separate building types with their own armour and strength (GATICK concrete 350, GAARTY light 300, DJUGG light 400 vs 350 mobile, GADPSA wood 600, MSTL wood 200); a game-wide trap for modes and armour notes.

Copy-check: three Nod unit names in the order of the Temple of Nod (Tiberian Sun) page (8 words) and the list of movement types with their damage shares from Rules.ini (6 words) would be FOUND lines; reword before committing.

Crate list misses the Invulnerability crate (Rules.ini [Powerups] Invulnerability=10).

candidates.name: Mutant Hijacker
candidates.teaches: hijack-vehicle, an id no researched unit links yet: an unarmed mutant commando who walks up to any enemy vehicle, from a buggy to the Mammoth Mk. II or an MCV, and takes it over. He is locked inside until that vehicle is destroyed, then climbs out on foot to go after the next one. One at a time, and he heals while standing in Tiberium. Iconic counter: one soldier can turn the enemy's single super-walker into his own.

new_mechanics.summary: A field that hurts others (Tiberium, radiation) heals you while you stand in it, so the hazard is your repair bay and your escape route.

candidates.repeats: No researched unit hijacks; docs/samples.md and the leech-weapon-on-kill pattern file name him only for contrast. Generals' GLA Hijacker (batch R3) teaches the same id and adds stealth while idle; this one adds the one-at-a-time cap and Tiberium healing.
candidates.skirmish: Yes, for Nod: Hand of Nod after the Temple of Nod (t3), $1850 (very high), one at a time. The Hand of Nod page marks him multiplayer only, and GDI gets him only in the campaign. The skirmish AI uses him, delivered by a Subterranean APC.
candidates.shooter_note: An unarmed runner who wins by touching an enemy vehicle: its driver is thrown out and he drives it until it dies, then he is back on foot hunting the next ride.

candidates.name: Cyborg
candidates.role_guess: assault (the Hand of Nod list calls it heavy assault infantry), anti-infantry as secondary
candidates.teaches: A crippled state no registry id covers: once badly hurt, the cyborg sheds its legs and keeps shooting while it crawls much slower, and repairs restore its health but never the legs. It is also armoured infantry (anti-tank weapons hurt it more than anti-infantry ones, and vehicles cannot run it over), heals while standing in Tiberium that harms other soldiers, and is shut down by EMP like a vehicle, so it is soldier and machine at once.

new_mechanics.summary: Below a health threshold you lose your legs for the rest of your life: you crawl at a fraction of your speed but keep fighting, and healing gives back health, not speed. The merge pass may make it an armour model.
A field that hurts others (Tiberium, radiation) heals you while you stand in it, so the hazard is your repair bay and your escape route.

candidates.repeats: Nothing in data/units has a crippled state; the nearest terms are the armour models downed-revive (only at zero health) and critical-burn (disabled until repaired). The Cyborg Commando has the same legs-off rule at hero tier. Tiberium healing is shared by every TS cyborg and mutant (Hijacker, Ghost Stalker, Reaper), so the game notes may call it game-wide.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Nod's heavy infantry from the Hand of Nod with no other building (t1), $650 (low), skirmish and multiplayer. Firestorm's campaign swaps in the Elite Cadre in places.
candidates.shooter_note: A tough trooper whose low-health state is a slow, crawling torso that still shoots: the enemy must finish him, and he can drag himself to a Tiberium patch to heal.

candidates.name: Subterranean APC
candidates.teaches: Travel under the map with passengers: five soldiers ride below ground, seen only by a deployed sensor array, past cliffs and base defences, and come up beside the target (the classic engineer raid on a Construction Yard). The counterplay is terrain: it cannot go down or come up through concrete paving, Tiberium fields or rough ground, so defenders pave their bases. It has no weapon.
candidates.repeats: burrow is linked by the RA1 Submarine (hides and surfaces in place) and carry-passengers by the RA3 Sudden Transport; this unit adds travelling under the ground. The burrow and carry-passengers pattern files already cite it as an other example (variants tunnel and tunnel-carrier), so coding it gives them a source unit. The Devil's Tongue tunnels the same way, and Tiberium Wars dropped tunnelling, so R2 has no other tunneller.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Nod War Factory after the Nod Tech Center (t3), skirmish and multiplayer; the skirmish AI uses it for raids. Price conflict: $800 in the wiki infobox, $600 on CNCNZ (medium against low band); check patch 2.03.
candidates.shooter_note: A driver who picks a surfacing spot and delivers a full squad inside the enemy base; the riders are safe and blind while under, and paving or a sensor is the answer.

candidates.name: Mobile Sensor Array
candidates.teaches: reveal-area as a parked post, the registry's own TS example: the truck must stop and deploy before its sensors work, then shows cloaked and tunnelling units and buildings around it on radar and on screen. They stay cloaked, so others must still attack them. It never shows on enemy radar and carries no gun. Firestorm's manual adds limpet drones and mines to what it finds, which makes it the hard counter to every Nod stealth trick on this list.
candidates.repeats: reveal-area is linked by the RA1 Spy through the one-shot sonar pulse it earns; this is the lasting, deploy-to-scan version, already the reveal-area pattern file's deployed-array example. Other TS detectors get the ability only from elite ranks or are buildings.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: both the GDI and Nod war factories build it after Radar (t2), $950 (medium), skirmish and multiplayer, so it is shared. The skirmish AI never builds it.
candidates.shooter_note: A support player who plants himself so the team can see and shoot the invisible; once he packs up to follow the push, the stealth comes back.

candidates.name: Mobile Stealth Generator
candidates.role_guess: buffer (it hides the allies around it); the wiki calls it a support vehicle
candidates.teaches: cloak for a whole group, which no researched unit links yet: an unarmed Firestorm truck that deploys to cloak every friendly unit and building in a bubble around it, cannot move while the bubble is up, and flickers when it takes hits. Two of them leapfrog to keep an army hidden while it advances. The Mobile Sensor Array is its counter.
candidates.repeats: The RA1 Mobile Gap Generator also hides allies around a truck, but with shroud while it drives (shroud-area, whose summary names cloak's area variant as the contrast). The TS Stealth Tank carries the personal cloak, a line TD, TW and Renegade also have; the group bubble is TS's own twist.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Nod, Firestorm only, War Factory after the Stealth Generator (t3), $1600 (very high, on the edge), skirmish and multiplayer. The skirmish AI does not use it.
candidates.shooter_note: A team-cloak player who must stand still to hide everyone near him: the squad hops between two bubbles, and taking fire makes his bubble flicker.

candidates.name: Limpet Drone
candidates.role_guess: scout (the wiki calls it a reconnaissance drone), disabler as secondary
candidates.teaches: A drone that is its own mine: it hovers out (water too), buries itself out of sight, latches under the first enemy vehicle to drive over it, slows it and shares what it sees with its owner until a service depot or mobile repair vehicle pulls it off. It does no damage; EMP destroys a deployed one and sensors reveal it.
candidates.repeats: infest-vehicle is linked by the RA3 Terror Drone sample, which destroys from inside; this one tracks and slows instead. The infest-vehicle pattern file already uses it as an other example (anchor, tracker and mine-latch variants), so coding it gives those variants a source unit.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Firestorm, built by both the GDI and Nod war factories after Radar (t2), $550 (low), skirmish and multiplayer, so it is shared. The AI never builds it.
candidates.shooter_note: A tiny drone player who hides on a road, then rides an enemy tank as a spy camera that slows it, until the enemy drives off for repairs.

candidates.name: Mobile EMP
candidates.teaches: disable-machine as a pulse that ignores sides: a quick, thin-skinned truck charges for a long time, then lets out a short-range pulse that shuts down every vehicle, cyborg and base defence around it, its own side's included, for a short time. It is immune to its own pulse but not to another's, infantry ignore it, and a second pulse does not lengthen the first. EMP also kills deployed limpets and drives tunnellers up, so it is the counter to Nod's cyborg and stealth tricks.
candidates.repeats: disable-machine is linked by the RA3 Terror Drone (a stun beam on one target); the pattern file already cites this unit as an other example (variants shutdown-pulse and charged-burst). The EMP Cannon support power is the building version. Id: the infobox and the Firestorm manual call it the Mobile EMP Cannon; settle the in-game name.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: GDI, Firestorm only, War Factory after the Electromagnetic Pulse Cannon (t2), $1000 (medium), skirmish and multiplayer. Unused by the AI.
candidates.shooter_note: Sneak in already charged, pop the pulse to freeze every machine nearby, then run; friendly vehicles in the circle freeze too, so the team must clear out first.

candidates.name: Jump Jet Infantry
candidates.role_guess: assault by the barracks list's airborne assault infantry label (check), with anti-air and raider as likely secondaries
candidates.teaches: Infantry in the low-air layer, the first unit for the jetpack mobility term: GDI soldiers fly over any terrain, touch down after every flight or kill, and walk short moves on foot. Their chain gun hits ground and air alike, and the counters the wiki lists are all anti-air units, so the switch between flying and standing decides who can hurt them. Firestorm adds stealth detection and faster flight.
candidates.repeats: No researched unit uses jetpack. The registry folds jump packs into leap, but this is lasting flight, not a hop, so the lesson rests on the mobility term rather than a pattern id.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: GDI Barracks after Radar (t2), $600 (low), skirmish and multiplayer.
candidates.shooter_note: A jetpack trooper who hovers and strafes over walls and cliffs, but must land to rest and is then a plain soldier; anti-air players are his hard counter.

candidates.name: Mobile War Factory (GDI) / Fist of Nod (Nod)
candidates.teaches: A forward factory on tracks: a slow, unarmed, heavily armoured Firestorm vehicle, one per player, that unfolds into a full war factory near the front and builds its side's normal vehicle list there. Once unfolded it cannot be repaired the usual way (only by a service depot or mobile repair vehicle), and an enemy engineer can capture it; a Carryall can airlift it. It brings host-spawn-point and the engineer role, which no researched unit covers.
candidates.repeats: The Slave Miner also unfolds into a building (deploy-siege-mode's become-structure variant), but a refinery; this one becomes a place new vehicles come from. MCVs do the same for a whole base and are skipped.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Firestorm, both sides (the manual lists it for GDI and Nod), one per player, $1800 (very high), skirmish and multiplayer; the AI never uses it. Gates: this page names the Upgrade Center for GDI and the Temple of Nod for Nod, while the Nod war factory page says Upgrade Center for the Fist (the registry note's open question); t3 either way. Decide shared against one entry per side (cnc-ts.gdi.mobile-war-factory, cnc-ts.nod.fist-of-nod), since each side's version builds its own arsenal.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow truck the team escorts to a safe spot, where it unfolds into a forward shop: teammates respawn there in vehicles, so killing or capturing it pushes the whole team back.

candidates.name: Orca Carryall
candidates.teaches: Airlifting a whole vehicle: an unarmed, fast, fragile aircraft that hooks any ground vehicle (a Titan, a Disruptor, an APC full of soldiers, even the Mobile War Factory or the Mammoth Mk. II), carries it over terrain and defences and sets it down where told; the drop point can change mid-flight. It cannot lift soldiers on their own.
candidates.repeats: carry-passengers is linked by the RA3 Sudden Transport (soldier seats). The pattern's airlift-vehicle variant cites only Red Alert 3, StarCraft II and Supreme Commander, so this would be its C&C source unit. TW's Nod Carryall continues the line.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: GDI Helipad, which also needs a Service Depot, $750 (medium), skirmish and multiplayer; unused by the AI. Tier: the gates give t2 (the Helipad; the Service Depot is not in the tier map), while the infobox says tier 3.
candidates.shooter_note: A sky-crane pilot who grabs a teammate's tank, with the teammate still driving, and drops it behind enemy lines; the pair are easy prey while airborne.

candidates.name: Disruptor
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (the wiki calls it an advanced anti-armour unit), siege as secondary (the factory list adds anti-structure)
candidates.teaches: A friendly-fire beam with one exception: the sonic wave runs through every unit and building in its line and harms friend and foe alike, except other Disruptors, which it cannot hurt, so they work best in packs. One wave can damage several buildings in a row and can set off blue Tiberium. It has no anti-air and a short reach, and dug-in Tick Tanks shrug it off.
candidates.repeats: No pattern fits: the lesson is at weapon-trait level (pierce and friendly-fire on the sonic family, terms the Multigunner IFV's rider weapons already use). The immunity of its own kind has no term: a word-list gap to report rather than a new pattern. The page also says the damage builds the longer a target stays in the wave; check it. Kane's Wrath's Shatterer continues the sonic line.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: GDI War Factory after the GDI Tech Center (t3), $1300 (high), skirmish and multiplayer.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow sonic tank whose beam cuts through everything in a line, teammates included unless they also drive Disruptors: a positioning puzzle for the whole team.

candidates.name: Mammoth Mk. II
candidates.role_guess: assault (the wiki's super-heavy assault walker), anti-air as secondary
candidates.teaches: The one-per-player super walker: a slow, four-legged giant and the game's dearest unit, with railguns that pierce rows of units but are stopped by terrain, and anti-air missiles; it never gains ranks. Its counters are memorable: a single Mutant Hijacker can steal it, dug-in Tick Tanks resist its railguns, and its slowness makes it artillery bait. It would be the first unit with availability limited and the railgun family.
candidates.repeats: Continues the Mammoth line that R1 kept as the RA1 Mammoth Tank; the twists are the walker body, the cap of one, piercing railguns and no ranks. TD's Mammoth and TW's Mammoth and MARV are the same line, so keep it once.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: GDI War Factory after the GDI Tech Center (t3), $3000 (very high), one at a time, skirmish and multiplayer. Patch 2.03 raised its health in the game code. The war factory list says it repairs itself, but the unit page mentions self-repair only in its background; check.
candidates.shooter_note: The team's walking fortress, one per team: huge line-piercing firepower, but so slow it needs escorts against aircraft and hijackers.

candidates.name: Tick Tank
candidates.teaches: A defensive deploy: Nod's main battle tank, the registry's cost anchor, digs its hull into the ground, cannot move until it digs out, and becomes far harder to hurt (light armour on the move, concrete dug in) with a full turret arc. Dug in it shrugs off the Disruptor's wave and the Mk. II's railguns; in the open the Titan beats it. Elite ranks add stealth detection, a second cannon and self-repair.
candidates.repeats: deploy-siege-mode already has three source units (Desolator, Siege Chopper, Slave Miner), which gain a zone, a long gun or a building; this one gains armour instead. The pattern file cites it as the dig-in variant's example. It is also the batch's t1 vehicle and the counter to two GDI candidates.
candidates.skirmish: Yes: Nod War Factory with no other building (t1), $800 (medium), skirmish and multiplayer.
candidates.shooter_note: A tank that digs in to become a hardened turret anywhere on the map, trading all movement for toughness; the moment it digs out is the window to punish it.

candidates.coverage_note: 13 candidates, all buildable in skirmish and multiplayer at patch 2.03 with Firestorm (4 are Firestorm units). Factions: Nod 5 (Mutant Hijacker, Cyborg, Subterranean APC, Mobile Stealth Generator, Tick Tank), GDI 5 (Jump Jet Infantry, Mobile EMP, Orca Carryall, Disruptor, Mammoth Mk. II), shared 3 (Mobile Sensor Array, Limpet Drone, and the Mobile War Factory, which Nod calls the Fist of Nod). Classes: infantry 3, vehicle 7, walker 1, aircraft 1 (low air, transport), drone 1 (hover, amphibious). TS has no ships, and its one hover tank (Hover MLRS) teaches nothing new. Tiers by the registry gates: t1 2, t2 5, t3 6. Prices: low 3, medium 5, high 1, very high 4; no very-low unit (light infantry, disc thrower) teaches anything. Role guesses: assault 4, transport 2 (one under the ground with soldiers, one by air with a vehicle), scout 2 (no researched unit is a scout first), and one each of infiltrator, buffer, disabler, engineer (none researched yet) and anti-armour. Ids: hijack-vehicle, cloak and host-spawn-point get their first source units; reveal-area gets the registry's own TS example; burrow (tunnel), carry-passengers (tunnel and vehicle airlift), infest-vehicle (tracker), lay-mines, disable-machine (a pulse that hits both sides) and deploy-siege-mode (dig-in, become-structure) get twists. R1's pattern files already cite six of these units as other examples, so coding them moves them into source_units. Proposed new ids: cripple-at-low-health and heal-in-hazard. Three picks link no id and stay for class or twist: Jump Jet Infantry (first jetpack), Disruptor (friendly fire that spares its own kind, a word-list gap) and Mammoth Mk. II (first limited vehicle and railgun). Left out on purpose: Cyborg Reaper (first alternate: a Nod walker whose net pins infantry), Stealth Tank (personal cloak; TD, TW and Renegade share the line), Devil's Tongue (same tunnel lesson), Juggernaut and Nod Artillery (deploy-to-fire repeats), Ghost Stalker and Cyborg Commando (one-per-player heroes repeating Tanya's C4 and the Cyborg's legs), Engineer (the TD and TW capture line), Weed Eater (gather-resources), Orca Fighter, Orca Bomber, Harpy and Banshee (rearming repeats the Yak), plain line units, campaign-only units (Chameleon Spy, Elite Cadre, Forgotten mutants) and support powers. Flags for researchers: Subterranean APC price ($800 wiki, $600 CNCNZ), Carryall tier (t2 by gates, infobox 3), the Fist of Nod's gate and shared against per-side ids, Mobile EMP's in-game name, Mk. II self-repair, Disruptor damage build-up. Across batches: Generals' GLA Hijacker (R3) also teaches hijack-vehicle; the Mammoth, stealth tank, engineer, Juggernaut and sonic lines recur in TD, TW and Renegade.
